additional_concerns: The source assigns continuing ultimate responsibility but supplies no complete test of effective retention or discharge through supervision. Governance, practical authority and conduct are possible evidence, not source-established necessary or sufficient conditions. Actual facts are absent.

Retention, supervisory conduct and outcomes must remain separate. The proper-records and operational-compatibility duty in s2 is substantive; neither successful operations alone prove retained accountability nor an operational failure alone proves its loss.

Paragraph 14 and footnote 5 must be read together. The main text attaches the request trigger directly to demonstration, leaving confirmation unconditioned. Footnote 5 specifies minimum compliance with paragraphs 10–13 and high confidence concerning smart-contract vulnerabilities, while its unqualified confirmation-and-demonstration wording leaves a possible tension about the demonstration trigger. The supplied material does not resolve that tension or clearly extend the SFC-satisfaction standard to confirmation.

Absent an SFC request, continuing responsibility and confirmation remain applicable. Paragraphs 15 and 16 expressly condition obtaining third-party audit or verification and a satisfactory legal opinion, respectively, on a request; their triggers do not suspend the underlying responsibility.

Section 6.11C concerns outsourced valuation and its specified management-company supervision duties. It does not establish a universal Product Provider retention or fulfillment test. Likewise, intermediary paragraphs 13 and 17–18 require their own actor and activity conditions.
No executable meaning is supplied. No finding here establishes an executable defect, a fulfilled requirement, or authority to prune supported but separately scoped duties.
